Kept alive by the fan recreation WeatherStar 4000+ (Mike Battaglia; maintained by netbymatt since 2020).
options.what_it_is: Signalwave is the vaporwave sub-genre made from distorted broadcast idents, and Wikipedia singles out The Weather Channel as its main source. Its picture is the automated local-forecast screen: chunky shadowed text on blue panels over an orange-and-purple gradient, cycling through pages of data. It is remembered as the calmest thing on 1990s television, and unlike most vaporwave imagery it is pure broadcast graphics with no photograph in it. The earlier research mentioned this only as a variant inside the VHS entry; it deserves its own entry.
visual_signature: 4:3 frame filled by a gradient running from dark indigo-purple at the top to burnt orange at the bottom, with a diagonal break near the top
A centred navy data panel about two-thirds of the frame wide with a lighter blue, soft-glowing border

Header row above the panel: a square logo tile at top left (blue with a white rounded outline), a two-line page title in yellow with a hard black drop shadow, and at top right a clock with seconds and a day-and-date line in white wide-tracked capitals
Data as label-and-value rows: labels left-aligned with a colon, values right-aligned, in chunky white condensed lettering with a 2-3px black drop shadow; the location name in yellow
One oversized reading at the top left of the panel with a one-word description under it, and beneath that a cartoon icon drawn with a thick black outline and flat yellow fill
A full-width navy crawl bar along the bottom edge carrying a single line of white text, separated from the picture by a thin lighter line

The screen works as a slideshow of named pages; the recreation lists Current Conditions, Latest Observations, Hourly, Local Forecast, Extended Forecast, Regional Forecast, Almanac, Travel, Radar and Hazards
options.palette: Sampled by me from the WeatherStar 4000+ project image (approximate): background top #180f57 to #38194a, background bottom #b9570d, panel #1e295a, panel border #1c4596, crawl bar #1e3470, title yellow (pure #ffff00 family), text white with black shadow. The project itself describes the look simply as blue and orange.
options.typography: A chunky condensed bitmap face with rounded terminals and a hard black drop shadow for data; a wide, extended capital face for the clock. The recreation uses fan-made 'Star4000' fonts credited to Nick Smith of TWCClassics. Mixed case for labels, capitals for the clock.
options.motion: Pages replace one another every 8-10 seconds with a hard cut; the bottom crawl scrolls right to left continuously; the clock ticks each second; an icon alternates between two frames. Calm and mechanical.

references.what: Vaporwave article, Signalwave section: samples radio, television and station idents, particularly from The Weather Channel; names Cat System Corp. and CT57
WeatherStar: history of the 4000 unit (1988 development, 1990 introduction, text over stylised graphical backgrounds, retired 2014)
WeatherStar 4000+ README: a fan recreation of the 1990s local forecast, its list of screens, font and icon credits, and its ownership disclaimer
WeatherStar 4000+ Current Conditions image, which I downloaded and viewed; the visual signature above describes this screen
News at 11 (Cat System Corp., 2016): tracks 10-20 built on Weather Channel samples; cover seen through the channel's old logo shape
Bandcamp Daily family tree: broken transmission / signalwave defined as piled-up radio and TV clips simulating channel-hopping

options.readme_translation: Animated SVG in a 4:3 frame. Page one is 'Current Conditions' for the repo: the oversized reading is the version or the star count, the label-and-value rows are real facts (language, licence, tests, last release), and the icon is an original drawing tied to the project. Page two is 'Local Forecast': the project description as a short paragraph. The bottom crawl carries the install command. The clock at top right can show the build date. Links go below in Markdown.
options.feasibility_notes: Everything is rects, two linear gradients and text. Panel glow: one feGaussianBlur on a stroked rect. Text shadow: a black copy of each text group offset 2-3px (no filter needed). Pages: groups with opacity keyframes using steps() so they cut rather than fade. Crawl: a text group translated inside a clipPath. The lettering carries the recognition, so it must be outlined paths or an embedded subset of an open-licence font with similar chunky proportions; a system sans-serif will not read as the style. Small and cheap to render (well under 40 KB).
options.caveats: Do not use The Weather Channel name or logo, the NOAA emblem, the phrase used for its forecast segment, or the fan-made Star4000 fonts (they replicate a proprietary broadcast typeface and their licence is unclear). The README of the recreation states the unit and technology belong to The Weather Channel. Free to reuse: gradient backdrop, blue panel, shadowed label-and-value rows, crawl bar, paged slideshow. I viewed only the Current Conditions screen; the layouts of the other pages are not described here because I did not see them. Yellow and white on navy pass contrast; keep the shadow. North American viewers will recognise it instantly, others less so.

options.name: Memphis: squiggles, confetti and laminate
options.era: Memphis Group founded by Ettore Sottsass in Milan on 6 December 1980; Sottsass left in 1985 and the group disbanded in 1987. Its graphics ran through pop culture from the mid 1980s to the mid 1990s and feed directly into vaporwave.
options.what_it_is: Postmodern Italian furniture design that became the wallpaper of a decade: clashing flat colours, asymmetric geometry and busy surface patterns on cheap plastic laminate. Sottsass's Bacterio squiggle print and the 1981 Carlton bookcase are the emblems. People remember it as the look of late-80s television sets, school folders and arcade carpets, and Wikipedia lists Memphis shapes among vaporwave's ingredients.
visual_signature: Scattered short squiggles, zigzags and confetti dashes at random angles over a flat ground, none touching
A dense field of small black worm-like marks on white or pastel (the manner of Sottsass's laminate print)
Primitive shapes overlapping off-grid: circles, quarter-circles, triangles, stepped stairs, thick striped bars
Black-and-white stripes or checks placed directly against saturated flat colour
Terrazzo: irregular angular chips of several colours on a pale ground
Hard offset drop shadows in solid black, 4-8px down and right; no gradients, no perspective
options.palette: Flat and clashing: primary red, yellow and blue with pink, teal, mint and black-and-white patterning. The sources describe the palette without hex values. A common '80s' swatch set from Gridfiti: #FF68A8, #64CFF7, #F7E752, #CA7CD8, #3968CB.
options.typography: Bold geometric sans capitals with letters individually tilted or coloured differently; heavy black outlines and offset shadows. Hand-cut and playful, never refined.
options.motion: Optional: shapes jiggle or rotate a few degrees on staggered loops; confetti drifts; stripes scroll inside their shapes; letters bounce in one by one. It works fully static.

references.what: Memphis Group: founding date, members, traits, influence on mid-80s to mid-90s pop culture, vaporwave and 'Corporate Memphis'
Ettore Sottsass: the Bacterio print and the Carlton bookcase (1981)
Abet Laminati: Bacterio is still sold as a current laminate, which is why it must not be copied
CARI on Global Village Coffeehouse, the late-80s to mid-90s style that softened Memphis squiggles (useful for telling the two apart)

options.readme_translation: SVG banner with a pastel ground covered in an original squiggle-and-confetti pattern, a few large overlapping primitives, and the project name in chunky tilted capitals with black offset shadows. Pattern tiles can be reused as section dividers. It needs a computing element (a window frame, a cursor, a floppy outline) to tie it to the tool.
options.feasibility_notes: Pure flat vector: one <pattern> tile of short stroked paths for the squiggle field, a handful of shapes with solid fills, striped fills through a second pattern. No filters or gradients, so it is small (under 20 KB) and renders identically everywhere. Lettering should be outlined. A generator can vary it per repo by seeding the scatter.
options.caveats: Do not reproduce Bacterio or other named Memphis patterns or furniture designs: Bacterio is a current commercial product of Abet Laminati. Draw your own squiggle tile; the general vocabulary is free. On its own it reads as 1980s children's television rather than computing, which is off-theme for a scene-flavoured tool. It tips easily into the much-mocked Corporate Memphis illustration style; avoid people figures. Bacterio is usually dated 1978, before the group formed; I saw that date only in search results, not on a page I opened.

options.name: Neon cube field: the rez-era Razor look
options.era: 2010-2012, Windows; Razor 1911 cracktros and 64k intros coded by rez with music by Dubmood (The Settlers 7 cracktro, 27 Apr 2010; StarCraft 2 cracktro, 31 July 2010; Insert No Coins, 2 Oct 2010; The Scene Is Dead, 8 Apr 2012). A DOS ancestor exists in Razor Crack Intro #13.
options.what_it_is: When Razor's demo section came back around 2010 it had a consistent look: fields of glowing rainbow cubes and glenz shapes, a pixel logo, scanlines and a Dubmood chiptune. Insert No Coins won the 64k competition at Main 2010 and the public-choice award at the Scene.org Awards; The Scene Is Dead placed third in PC 64k at Revision 2012. For many people this is 'the Razor 1911 one'. The rainbow-cubes idea is older than rez's use of it: the undated DOS Crack Intro #13 already shows a 9x7 grid of cubes, one hue per cube.
visual_signature: Hundreds of small cubes in a regular grid, each a different hue, so the field reads as a continuous rainbow ramp
The field bent into a tunnel, a rolling wave landscape, or a wall seen in perspective (the four panels of the Insert No Coins screenshot)
Glow on everything against near-black
A segmented, LCD-like pixel wordmark pinned to the top centre of the frame (logo by iLKke on Insert No Coins)
Rows of small translucent glenz polyhedra ordered by hue behind a rainbow block-letter logo, under horizontal scanlines (Settlers 7 cracktro)
Text as three-dimensional ASCII characters and a rotating 3D ASCII logo, a starfield with a cube, turning cogs and a sine scroller (StarCraft 2 cracktro, per comments)
CRT treatment: scanlines, vignette and phosphor glow, which several commenters found overdone (The Scene Is Dead)
DOS ancestor: flat-shaded rainbow cubes in a grid with the logo running vertically down the left edge (#13)
options.palette: Near-black background with a full-spectrum hue ramp at high saturation across the field. The Scene Is Dead narrows to amber, cyan and magenta on black (Vivian Voss's write-up).
options.typography: A pixel wordmark built from segments; body text in a small square bitmap font in white or pale cyan; extruded ASCII characters in the StarCraft 2 cracktro; text-writer delivery.
options.motion: From comments and stills: camera travel through or over the cube field, cubes rippling in a wave, glenz objects spinning, text typing on, scanlines fixed on top. Not watched.

references.what: Insert No Coins on Demozoo: 2 Oct 2010, 1st at Main 2010, code rez, logo Ilkke, music Dubmood, public-choice award, source available
Insert No Coins on Pouet: four-panel screenshot (cube tunnel, rainbow wave landscape)
StarCraft 2 cracktro on Pouet (July 2010; code rez, graphics kenet, music W.O.T.W. with a Dubmood remix): comments on the 3D ASCII, starfield with cube, sine scroller, cogs
The Settlers 7 Cracktro on Pouet (Apr 2010): rainbow logo over rows of glenz shapes; the ACiD logo dispute in the comments
Same on Demozoo: 27 Apr 2010, code and graphics rez, music Dubmood (and zabutom, uncredited)
The Scene Is Dead on Pouet (Apr 2012, 3rd in PC 64k at Revision): comments on the CRT filter
Vivian Voss on The Scene Is Dead: CRT post-processing, amber/cyan/magenta on black, rez and Dubmood
Razor Crack Intro #13 (DOS): grid of rainbow cubes with a vertical logo; undated on Pouet

options.readme_translation: SVG hero about 800x340 on black: an isometric field of small cubes rippling in a sine wave with the hue sweeping across it, the project wordmark as a segmented pixel logo at the top centre, one line of text typing on, scanlines over everything. Install line and links below in Markdown.
options.feasibility_notes: A fixed isometric view is practical: emit a 16x8 grid of cubes (three polygons each: top, left and right faces at three lightness levels of the cube's hue), give every cube the same translateY keyframe with a negative delay derived from its grid position so a wave travels across, and set hues statically by column. About 400 polygons and one keyframe, 60-120 KB; reduce to 12x6 to halve it. Scanlines: a 2px pattern overlay. Vignette: a radial gradient. Glow: a single static blurred duplicate layer at most; an animated blur over 400 moving shapes is too expensive. The camera fly-through and cube tunnel of the originals would need per-frame geometry and exceed the budget: not possible as such.
options.caveats: Do not copy Razor's pixel wordmark (a credited artist's logo) or the name. The rainbow block logo in the Settlers 7 cracktro is, according to Pouet comments by ACiD's radman and by rez, an ACiD text-art logo by JED from 1996 reused with an altered signature, which drew an objection: a concrete example of why borrowed logos must be avoided. Cube fields, glenz and scanlines are generic. #13's date is unconfirmed (none on Pouet; Demozoo says 1994, which sits oddly with the 1996-98 numbering). Wow lowered from 5 to 4 because the buildable version is a static-camera cube wave without bloom. Saturated rainbow motion across the full width is tiring: keep amplitude and speed low, freeze under prefers-reduced-motion, and test scrolling on a phone.

selection_scope: Exclude every previous MediaLog style. References used for other projects may recur; all emblems are new. The earlier globally unused graphic pool has fewer than twenty options.

user_overrides.wordmark: Consistent plain sans-serif, no scene lettering
user_overrides.art: Original graphic symbols, no ASCII, gentle book/diary preference, restrained accents
